anti_patterns: Treating blobs as permanent storage: posting records with no offchain archival and expecting L1 retrieval after the ~18-day window
Reading blob bytes from the EVM: contracts can only see the versioned hash and call the point-evaluation precompile, never the blob body
Using blobs for small high-value state transitions where calldata or direct execution is simpler and permanence matters
Ignoring blob-gas dynamics: assuming flat fees when the exponential update rule can raise prices ~1.125x per block under congestion
Skipping KZG verification on the consumer side: trusting sequencer-posted data without checking commitments via the precompile or proofs
avoid_when: Consumers need permanent onchain retrievability beyond the ~4096-epoch (~18-day) pruning window
Smart contracts must read the posted data at execution time (blobs are invisible to the EVM)
Data volumes are small enough that calldata simplicity outweighs blob plumbing
Strict data-residency rules forbid propagation to a global validator set
Single-organization system with no multi-party availability dispute to resolve
benefits: Much cheaper rollup data availability than calldata: blob gas trades on its own EIP-1559-style fee market, decoupled from execution gas, with very low fees while blob usage is limited
No permanent state bloat: blobs live on the consensus layer only and prune after ~4096 epochs (~18 days), so L1 pays for an availability window instead of eternal storage
Forward-compatible path to full danksharding: type-0x03 format, KZG commitments, and sidecar propagation are the same constructs full sharding will use, so rollups upgrade once
Verifiable without execution: KZG commitments plus the point-evaluation precompile (0x0A) let optimistic and ZK provers check blob data without EVM access to it
Bounded worst-case bandwidth: target 3 blobs (0.375 MB) and max 6 blobs (0.75 MB) per block cap the extra load consensus nodes must download
best_practices: Run dedicated blob archival: mirror every blob your system depends on into offchain storage before the pruning window closes
Verify commitments, don't trust sequencers: check versioned hashes via the point-evaluation precompile or KZG proofs on the consumer/prover side
Monitor the blob-gas market separately from execution gas: alert on excess_blob_gas growth, which compounds fees exponentially
Design for the window, not the chain: derive rollup state and complete fraud/validity challenges inside the ~18-day availability period
Pin commitment-scheme agility: consume versioned hashes opaquely so a future switch (e.g. Merkle plus STARK) only changes the sequencer path
Batch toward full 128 KB blobs where latency allows: underfilled blobs still consume the full per-blob gas
component_types: Blob-Carrying Transaction (type-0x03): execution-layer envelope holding blob_versioned_hashes and max_fee_per_blob_gas, never the blob bytes
Blob Sidecar: consensus-layer propagation unit carrying the 128 KB blob (4096 field elements of 32 bytes) alongside the beacon block
KZG Commitment Store: versioned hashes anchoring each blob onchain as permanent fossils after pruning
Blob-Gas Fee Market: independent EIP-1559-style pricer driven by excess_blob_gas with ~1.125x max per-block adjustment
Point-Evaluation Precompile (0x0A, 50000 gas): execution-layer verifier binding a claimed value to a versioned hash for optimistic and ZK rollups
Offchain Archiver: rollup-operator or third-party store preserving blob history past the pruning horizon
Prover/Challenger: honest actor re-executing blob data inside the availability window to verify or dispute state transitions
context: Ethereum L2 rollups must post their compressed batch data to L1 so any honest prover can reconstruct state and challenge fraud, but posting as calldata is expensive: every byte is executed by all nodes and stored forever, even though rollups only need availability for a bounded dispute window. EIP-4844 (proto-danksharding, live on mainnet with the Dencun upgrade in March 2024) adds a temporary-data lane: sequencers sign type-0x03 blob-carrying transactions that reference large blobs (~128 KB each, 4096 32-byte field elements) propagated as consensus-layer sidecars. Only the KZG commitment's versioned hash touches execution state; the EVM can verify points via the point-evaluation precompile but never reads blob bytes. Blobs price on an independent blob-gas market (target 3, max 6 per block) and prune after ~4096 epochs (~18 days), leaving only the commitment fossil onchain. Use this pattern when designing rollup data-availability posting, windowed DA layers, or any L1-anchored system that needs cheap, verifiable, time-boxed availability rather than permanent storage.
design_principles: Pay for availability windows, not eternity: price data by how long provers need it, then prune
Separate data-availability pricing from execution pricing so DA demand cannot crowd out computation
Commit onchain, reveal offchain: anchor succinct KZG commitments where execution can verify them, circulate bulk bytes where only availability matters
Keep bulk data out of the execution environment: invisibility to the EVM is what makes blobs cheap
Ship the end-state format early: adopt the exact transaction and commitment format full sharding will use so consumers upgrade once
Bound per-block externalities: hard-cap sidecar bandwidth so home operators can keep validating

references: Vitalik Buterin, Dankrad Feist, Diederik Loerakker, George Kadianakis, Matt Garnett et al., EIP-4844: Shard Blob Transactions, 2022 — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4844

technology_stack: Ethereum execution clients (type-0x03 blob transactions, 0x0A point-evaluation precompile)
Ethereum consensus clients (blob sidecar propagation and attestation)
Optimistic rollup stacks (post batches as blobs, verify via precompile)
ZK rollup stacks (KZG-friendly commitment checks in validity proofs)
tradeoffs: Time-boxed availability: after ~18 days blobs vanish from consensus nodes, so permanent history requires operator-run archival
EVM-invisible payloads: contracts cannot read blob contents, only versioned hashes, limiting onchain composability with posted data
Separate volatile fee market: blob-gas spikes exponentially under sustained over-target demand, so DA costs are cheap-but-bursty
All-nodes-download interim: until data-availability sampling lands, every consensus node fetches every sidecar, capping throughput at 6 blobs per block
Trusted-setup dependency: KZG commitments rest on the ceremony's powers-of-tau; a compromised setup would undermine commitment soundness
New operational surface: sequencers must manage blob construction, KZG proving, versioned-hash tracking, and archival in addition to batching
use_cases: Optimistic rollup batch posting: sequencer publishes compressed L2 batches as blobs for the fraud-proof window
ZK rollup data availability: publishing witness data blobs alongside validity proofs for independent reconstruction
L2 fee reduction: moving DA spend from calldata to the cheaper blob-gas market and passing savings to users
Windowed audit anchoring: committing data fingerprints onchain while bulk evidence circulates offchain during review
Staging lane toward full danksharding: building DA pipelines on the final transaction and commitment format ahead of DAS
